newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares sink on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares sink on profit-taking.

text.p: Chilean investors skimmed off profits after a series of bullish sessions, sending the blue- chip index falling in what brokers called a technical retreat.
The IPSA index closed 0.64 percent down at 111.41 points. The all-share IGPA ended 0.29 percent lower at 5249.93 points on so-so volume of 12 billion pesos.

Brokers said the bourse's bullish factors remained -- expectations of a Central Bank rate cut, strong foreign buying, good prospects for economic growth at home and in Argentina -- and that shares could regain ground Friday.

They noted an uneven performance among Chilean-issued American Depositary Receipts as another factor nudging down the IPSA. Risers included power utility Edelnor, up 4.6 percent to 181 pesos after it signed as a client on with the Atacama natural gas pipeline.

Endesa, one of two leading partners planning to build the Atacama project, was up one percent to 251 pesos. Endesa and its partner CMS Energy announced plans to build three new power plants in nothern Chile.
Decliners included Cruz Blanca, off 2.2 percent to 132 pesos and Andina, down three percent to 2,100 pesos.
